entry_conditions: Accept the demonstrated open, closing, loaded, or opening predecessor states, rather than initializing contact as empty. Supply two consecutive causal 20 Hz observations when possible: qpos fingers at indices 7:9 in metres, finger qvel at 16:18 in metres/second, world TCP pose 18:25, red pose 25:32, blue pose 32:39 and goals 41:47, with wxyz quaternions. In demo10000/504 the close command is -1 but both fingers remain about 0.04 m; /505 is about 0.0205 m with rapid negative finger motion; /506 is about 0.0183 m with blue still near table height. Recurrent entry /265 has red still held over its pad, z about 0.2085 m, while blue remains on the table. The model infers role context from both colors and goal relations; the actual forward signature has no role IDs or executed-command channel. Caller knowledge of the demonstrated red-first/blue-second context is therefore important. A repeated snapshot is a supported training augmentation but materially weaker evidence than two actual consecutive frames.
exit_conditions: Prefer transfer to delivery after observed intended-object lift toward the demonstrated world z near 0.28 m, maintained narrow fingers near 0.0183 m each, and a small stable TCP-object relative transform across actual motion. During the demonstrated grasp, TCP and object centers are nearly level with an approximately 8-10 mm lateral offset; there is no imposed vertical grasp offset. The block must be seen leaving its z near 0.02 m support region with the TCP: neither narrow fingers nor a -1 command alone establishes grasp. Demo10000/170,184 and /570, plus demo10011/560,583, support high lift and initial transport with closure maintained. These are qualitative readiness cues, not hard learned thresholds or a new success predicate. Transfer may occur earlier in pickup overlap only when the successor will continue verification and lift. Maintain the grasp through transfer, with no automatic open/reset pulse.
overlap_role: This policy learns the full expanded ranges, including open approach, closure lag, initial object lift and grasp-maintaining transport in the shared pickup intervals. It also learns the reverse red-loaded-to-empty transition and subsequent blue approach in the long recurrent overlap. For demo10000 the overlaps are [80,185), [265,425), and [470,585); all other assigned expanded ranges are retained as listed in PRIOR.md. During recurrent overlap the learned diffusion must finish goal-aligned red lowering, command opening, wait through physical separation as demonstrated, retreat while red remains supported, and then approach blue. No command sequence is scripted. Per-finger aperture and velocity, world goal proximity, TCP/object co-motion and separation distinguish a still-held predecessor from an empty retreat. A single observation of red above its goal is not sufficient readiness for requested blue acquisition.
successor_readiness: Pass the two most recent raw causal observations without a reset motion; preserve caller-side role and executed-command context if the successor interface can use it. A successor can recompute readiness from finger opening and relative object/TCP motion without consuming our latent. Our six-mode belief and gripper probability sequence are internal learned conditioning and are not an exported handoff API or calibrated contact measurement. This model itself receives no role IDs or executed-command history. Near pickup, the successor should tolerate uncertain closure and continue verifying actual lift. After predecessor release, supported stationary red near its goal with opening/open fingers and rising or departing TCP is evidence that an empty blue approach is physically possible. Do not treat the source command change as immediate physical release.
failure_signatures: Reassess if the caller infers loaded contact while the block stays at support height, TCP/object separation grows during attempted lift, repeated gripper reversals appear, or observed motion continually disagrees with the inferred contact phase. Opposing nonzero finger qvel is present in successful loaded grasps and is not by itself a failure. Insufficient history or an incorrect assumed predecessor can make normal release look like a failed grasp. There are no force labels and no demonstrated missed-grasp/slip recoveries, so these are diagnostic hypotheses, not a tested recovery mechanism or autonomous stop rule.
continuation_guidance: Continue acquisition while closure has not yet produced observed lift, while high transport is still being established, or while the predecessor remains held during goal-aligned descent/release/retreat. At each framework replan the policy reconstructs its belief from the supplied two observations and denoises a horizon-16 action chunk; the fixed execution prefix is eight. It has no cross-call recurrent cache and no every-observation command-history updater. Let the inference API choose invocation duration based on actual state, not a fixed source index or schedule. An early successor in shared pickup must finish verification/lift; a late successor should preserve closure. Once the required blocks satisfy the supplied red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal containment/z contract, do not impose an additional release, clearance, speed, or sustained-hold requirement merely to satisfy this handoff guidance.
limitations: Observed support includes successful pickup and predecessor release only. Mode targets are weak supervision from measured geometry/motion and demonstrated commands with masked future lift confirmation used only during training. The model is a learned eight-channel diffusion policy, not a finite-state controller: its probabilistic binary gripper head conditions the DDPM and does not override the continuous sampled command. No hard contact guarantee, exact binary output guarantee, IK, image encoder, kinematic constraint, arbitrary role ordering or validated failure recovery is implemented. The original stronger heuristic requested persistent history and executed commands; this two-observation, no-role interface implements a narrower causal approximation, documented in PRIOR.md. A single snapshot and unseen request ordering are weaker applicability cases. Training start/end measurements and these citations are evidence, not policy performance feedback.
